mainTopic: Interrupting קריאת שמע and הלל, tasting on a fast, and putting תפילה before greetings and business
overview: The גמרא finishes its fuller reading of the משנה about greeting people during קריאת שמע. It brings a ברייתא with the views of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה that supports this reading. רבי חייא rules that one may interrupt הלל and מגילה to greet someone. רבה adds that how much you may interrupt depends on whether it is a day when the full הלל is said. רבי אמי rules that a person who is fasting may taste food, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי tasted up to a רביעית. רב and שמואל teach from a פסוק in ישעיהו that you should not go out of your way to greet someone before praying. Other אמוראים add that taking care of your own affairs before תפילה is forbidden, and that one who prays first will have his needs cared for by ה׳. After a short side teaching about dreams, the גמרא returns to the משנה and rules like רבי יהודה that one may not stop between אלהיכם and אמת ויציב. It then begins to give his source from a פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the corrected reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The last line of the גמרא's fuller reading of the משנה: at the breaks between paragraphs, one greets out of respect and answers anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at the breaks between the paragraphs, he may greet someone out of respect and may answer a greeting from any person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its fixed-up reading of רבי יהודה's view in the משנה. At the breaks between paragraphs, the rules are more relaxed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the משנה seemed hard to understand. The גמרא solved it by saying the משנה is missing words. This line is the end of those missing words: at the breaks you may start a greeting out of respect and answer a greeting from anyone at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The breaks between the paragraphs of שמע

phrases.english: And at the breaks between the paragraphs
he may greet out of respect
and answer a greeting to any person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַפְּרָקִים שׁוֹאֵל מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד וּמֵשִׁיב שָׁלוֹם לְכׇל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'missing words' answer the גמרא gave just before this line
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה as written seemed hard to make sense of in רבי יהודה's view
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the missing words are added, רבי יהודה's view is clear: in the middle, greet out of fear and answer out of respect. At the breaks, greet out of respect and answer anyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the reading: רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same argument. רבי מאיר says that at the breaks you greet out of respect, and in the middle you greet out of fear. Answering is allowed in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: Someone reading שמע who met his teacher or someone greater than him may greet him out of respect at the breaks. Needless to say, he may answer. In the middle he may greet out of fear. Needless to say, he may answer. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the fuller reading of the משנה is correct. This step gives רבי מאיר's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows greeting at the breaks for respect and in the middle only for fear. He reasons that if you may start a greeting, you can surely answer one. So answering is always allowed wherever greeting is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
Out of fear (of a powerful person)
Needless to say, it is obvious

phrases.english: This was also taught in a baraita:
One who is reading Shema
and his teacher met him
or someone greater than him,
at the breaks, he greets out of respect
and needless to say, he may answer;
and in the middle, he greets out of fear
and needless to say, he may answer.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source that matches the fuller reading of the משנה
steps.raayaObject: The fuller reading of the משנה with the added words
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lays out the argument in full

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says: in the middle, greet out of fear and answer out of respect. At the breaks, greet out of respect and answer anyone. These are exactly the words the גמרא added to the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: In the middle, one greets out of fear and answers out of respect. At the breaks, one greets out of respect and answers a greeting from any person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's side, and it matches the גמרא's fixed-up משנה word for word. This proves the reading was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is a little more lenient than רבי מאיר about answering. In the middle you may answer out of respect, not only out of fear. At the breaks you may answer anyone, even a regular person. These are the exact words the גמרא said were missing from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: To any person, even an ordinary one

steps.whatToRemember: Two levels of break: in the middle of a paragraph, only fear (and for רבי יהודה, respect when answering). At the breaks between paragraphs, respect, and for רבי יהודה you may answer anyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'greeting first' (שואל) with 'answering' (משיב). Answering is always treated more leniently than starting a greeting.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
in the middle, he greets out of fear
and answers out of respect;
and at the breaks, he greets out of respect
and answers a greeting to any person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the second opinion, which is the part that proves the reading
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view as the גמרא filled it in
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the ברייתא, which matches word for word

steps.title: אחי asks: may one interrupt הלל and מגילה?
steps.stepSummary: אחי, the תנא of רבי חייא's study hall, asks רבי חייא whether one may interrupt הלל or the reading of the מגילה to greet someone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחי, the תנא of רבי חייא's study hall, asked רבי חייא: May one interrupt during הלל and the מגילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to a new question: do the rules for interrupting שמע also apply to הלל and מגילה? This step sets up the question, and the next step gives the two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we learned when you may stop in the middle of שמע to greet someone. Now אחי asks about two other readings, הלל and מגילה. These are different because they are about thanking ה' for miracles.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question needing an answer)
Here: the person who memorized and recited ברייתות in the study hall
The praise psalms said on holidays
The scroll of אסתר read on פורים

phrases.english: Achai asked
the tanna of the study hall of Rabbi Chiya
from Rabbi Chiya:
During Hallel and the Megillah,
what is the law, may one interrupt?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַחַי תַּנָּא דְבֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the interrupting rules of שמע and asks whether they apply to other readings
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether interrupting to greet is allowed during הלל and מגילה

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: One side: a קל וחומר from שמע, which comes from the Torah, so surely you may stop during הלל, which is only rabbinic. Other side: maybe פרסומי ניסא (making the miracle known) is more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say a קל וחומר: קריאת שמע is from the Torah and you may interrupt it, so surely you may interrupt הלל, which is only rabbinic? Or maybe making the miracle known is more important?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אחי was unsure by showing both sides of his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side uses a קל וחומר: if the stricter מצוה‎ (שמע, from the Torah) may be interrupted, the lighter one (הלל, rabbinic) surely may. The second side says הלל and מגילה have a special purpose, making the miracle known. That purpose might make them too important to interrupt, even though they are only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a stricter case to a lighter case
Is it even a question? (surely so)
Making the miracle known to the public

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rabbinic מצוה can sometimes be stricter than a Torah one, when it has a special purpose like making the miracle known.

phrases.english: Do we say a kal vachomer:
Shema, which is from the Torah, one may interrupt;
Hallel, which is rabbinic, is it even a question?!
Or perhaps publicizing the miracle is more important.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two reasons behind אחי's question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which matters more: the קל וחומר from a Torah מצוה, or the special importance of פרסומי ניסא

steps.title: רבי חייא answers: one may interrupt
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that one may interrupt הלל and מגילה, and there is nothing wrong with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: One may interrupt, and there is nothing wrong with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers אחי's question: yes, you may interrupt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא goes with the קל וחומר side. פרסומי ניסא does not make הלל and מגילה stricter than שמע when it comes to interrupting.

keyTerms.meaning: There is nothing wrong with it

phrases.english: He said to him: one interrupts,
and there is nothing wrong with that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ פּוֹסֵק וְאֵין בְּכָךְ כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question just asked
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Interrupting הלל and מגילה is allowed; the קל וחומר from שמע wins

steps.title: רבה's distinction between kinds of הלל days
steps.stepSummary: רבה says: on days when an individual says the complete הלל, one may stop between paragraphs but not in the middle. On days when the complete הלל is not said, one may stop even in the middle of a paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: On days when an individual completes the הלל, one may interrupt between paragraphs but not in the middle of a paragraph. On days when an individual does not complete the הלל, one may interrupt even in the middle of a paragraph.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds detail to רבי חייא's answer. How much you may interrupt depends on what kind of day it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On days when the full הלל is said, הלל is a real obligation, so you may stop only at the breaks between paragraphs, not in the middle. On days when the full הלל is not said, it is lighter, so you may stop even in the middle of a paragraph.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual praying on his own
Between one paragraph and the next

steps.whatToRemember: Full-הלל days: stop only between paragraphs. Days without full הלל: you may stop even in the middle of a paragraph.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the practical guide for when you may speak during הלל, based on how serious the obligation is that day.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:

phrases.aramaic: יָמִים שֶׁהַיָּחִיד גּוֹמֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַהַלֵּל,
phrases.english: Days on which an individual completes the Hallel,
between one paragraph and the next, he may interrupt;
in the middle of the paragraph, he may not interrupt;

phrases.aramaic: וְיָמִים שֶׁאֵין הַיָּחִיד גּוֹמֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַהַלֵּל —
phrases.english: and days on which an individual does not complete the Hallel,
he may interrupt even in the middle of the paragraph.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה יָמִים שֶׁהַיָּחִיד גּוֹמֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַהַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to רבי חייא's general permission by splitting it by type of day
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On full-הלל days, interrupt only between paragraphs. On days without full הלל, interrupt even mid-paragraph.

steps.title: רבינא did not stop הלל for רב בר שבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה with a story: on a day without the complete הלל, רבינא did not stop to greet רב בר שבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רב בר שבא once come to רבינא on a day when the complete הלל is not said, and רבינא did not stop for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's rule from Step 7 with a story about רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said that on days without the complete הלל you may stop even in the middle of a paragraph. Here רבינא did not stop to greet רב בר שבא on exactly such a day. That seems to show stopping is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of days. This story took place on the easier kind of day, when you may stop even in the middle of a paragraph. That is what makes the challenge strong.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav bar Shaba
happen to come before Ravina,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָמִים שֶׁאֵין הַיָּחִיד גּוֹמֵר אֶת הַהַלֵּל הֲוָה,
phrases.english: and it was one of the days when an individual does not complete Hallel,
and he did not stop for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's rule from Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that on days without the complete הלל one may stop even mid-paragraph
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבינא, on such a day, did not stop to greet רב בר שבא. That suggests stopping is not permitted.

steps.title: רב בר שבא was not important to רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The story is different: רבינא did not consider רב בר שבא important, so he did not stop for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב בר שבא is different, because he was not important in רבינא's eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining why רבינא did not stop in this one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story does not show that stopping is forbidden. רבינא simply did not see רב בר שבא as someone important enough to stop for. רבה's rule stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule still stands. Being allowed to stop does not mean you must stop for everyone, and רבינא did not stop for someone he did not see as important.

phrases.english: Rav bar Shaba is different
since he was not considered important to Ravina.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: the person was not important
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא's not stopping proves that stopping is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא did not stop only because רב בר שבא was not important to him, so רבה's rule stands

steps.title: May someone who is fasting taste food?
steps.stepSummary: אשיאן, the תנא of רבי אמי's study hall, asks רבי אמי whether a person who is fasting may taste food.
steps.simpleTranslation: אשיאן, the תנא of the study hall of רבי אמי, asked רבי אמי: may a person who is fasting taste food?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. Like אחי's question to רבי חייא in Step 4, a תנא asks his teacher a question, this time about tasting food on a fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether just tasting food counts as breaking a fast. The two sides of the question come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who memorized and recited teachings in the study hall
One who is in the middle of a fast

phrases.english: Ashyan asked
the tanna of the study hall of Rabbi Ami
of Rabbi Ami:
One who is fasting, may he taste?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַשְׁיָאן תַּנָּא דְבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, placed here because it is another question a תנא asked his teacher
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person who is fasting may taste food

steps.title: Eating and drinking, or any pleasure?
steps.stepSummary: The two sides: maybe he only took on not eating and drinking, and tasting is not that. Or maybe he took on not having any pleasure from food, and tasting does give pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he take on himself not to eat and drink? Tasting is not eating and drinking. Or maybe he took on himself not to have pleasure from food, and tasting does give pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible ways to understand what the person took on when he started fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on what a fast means. If it means no eating and drinking, tasting is fine, because tasting is not real eating. If it means no pleasure from food, tasting is forbidden, because it gives some pleasure.

phrases.english: Did he take upon himself not to eat and drink —
and that is not present here.
phrases.notes: Just tasting is not real eating or drinking.

phrases.english: Or perhaps he took upon himself to avoid pleasure —
and that is present here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a fast forbid only eating and drinking, or any pleasure from food?

steps.title: רבי אמי: he may taste
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that a person who is fasting may taste, and there is nothing wrong with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: he tastes, and there is nothing wrong with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question: tasting during a fast is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי allows tasting, so tasting does not break the fast. This fits the first side of the question: the person took on not eating and drinking, and tasting is not eating or drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: There is nothing wrong with it

phrases.english: He said to him:
He tastes, and there is nothing wrong with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: טוֹעֵם וְאֵין בְּכָךְ כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Steps 10-11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person who is fasting may taste food, and it does not matter

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that tasting does not need a ברכה, and that a person who is fasting may taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: tasting does not need a ברכה, and one who is fasting may taste, and there is nothing wrong with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the exact words of רבי אמי: 'טועם ואין בכך כלום.' It also adds a related rule, that tasting a dish does not need a ברכה. Both rules treat tasting as less than real eating.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא
Tasting food, such as checking a cooked dish

steps.whatToRemember: A person who is fasting may taste food, and tasting does not need a ברכה. Both רבי אמי and the ברייתא say so.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
Tasting does not require a blessing,
and one who is fasting
tastes, and there is nothing wrong with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אמי's answer in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's ruling that one who is fasting may taste
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording: מטעמת אינה טעונה ברכה, והשרוי בתענית טועם ואין בכך כלום

steps.title: How much may a fasting person taste?
steps.stepSummary: Since a fasting person may taste, the גמרא asks what the limit is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to how much may he taste?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about how much a fasting person is allowed to taste. This sets up the next step, which gives the amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 and step 13 said that tasting is allowed on a fast. Tasting cannot mean any amount, or it would just be eating. So the גמרא wants a clear limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to how much? What is the limit?

phrases.english: Up to how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how much may a person who is fasting taste, going back to step 12 and step 13.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the ruling that a fasting person may taste by asking for the exact limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum amount a fasting person may taste.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי tasted up to a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: The limit comes from what רבי אמי and רבי אסי did: they tasted up to a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי would taste up to the amount of a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with what two great אמוראים actually did. When they fasted, they tasted up to a רביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not a stated rule. It is learned from what רבי אמי and רבי אסי did. That sets the amount for tasting at a רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: A רביעית, a quarter of a לוג

steps.whatToRemember: A fasting person may taste, up to a רביעית, based on what רבי אמי and רבי אסי did.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
would taste up to the amount of a quarter [of a log].
phrases.notes: A לוג is a liquid measure, and a רביעית is a quarter of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי טָעֲמִי עַד שִׁיעוּר רְבִיעֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to a רביעית, based on what רבי אמי and רבי אסי did.

steps.title: Greeting someone before praying is like building an altar
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that greeting a friend before praying is as if one made him into a בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Anyone who greets his friend before he has prayed, it is as if he made him into an altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב says that greeting another person before תפילה in the morning is like building a בָּמָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is about priority. The first honor of the day belongs to ה׳, so giving it to a person first is described very harshly, as if one built an altar to him. The source comes in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic. It is not connected to the fasting discussion before it.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Anyone who greets his friend
before he has prayed,
it is as if he made him an altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כָּל הַנּוֹתֵן שָׁלוֹם לַחֲבֵירוֹ קוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the fasting discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greeting a friend before praying is like building a בָּמָה.

steps.title: רב's source: reading בַּמֶּה as בָּמָה
steps.stepSummary: רב brings a פסוק from ישעיהו and reads the word בַּמֶּה ("how little") as בָּמָה (altar).
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Stop relying on man, who has only breath in his nostrils, for how little is he worth." Do not read it as בַּמֶּה (how little), but as בָּמָה (altar).
steps.whatsHappening: רב shows where his teaching comes from. He reads one word of the פסוק with different vowels to find his lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "breath in his nostrils" point to a person just waking up in the morning. By reading בַּמֶּה as בָּמָה, the פסוק warns that turning first to such a person makes him into a בָּמָה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as written, but as another reading

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Cease you from man,"
in whose nostrils there is breath,
for how little is he to be accounted."
Do not read it as bameh, 'how,'
but rather as bamah, 'altar.'
phrases.notes: Both words have the same letters. Only the vowels change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רב's statement in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that greeting before praying is like building a בָּמָה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 2:22, with the word בַּמֶּה read as בָּמָה.

steps.title: שמואל reads the same פסוק in its plain way
steps.stepSummary: שמואל keeps the word as בַּמֶּה and reads it as a rebuke: why did you value this person and not ה׳?
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: How did you consider this person important, and not ה׳?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains the same פסוק differently. He keeps the plain reading בַּמֶּה ("how") and turns it into a question of rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב changed the vowels to get בָּמָה, but שמואל does not change the reading. He reads the פסוק as asking why a person was given importance before ה׳. Both reach a similar lesson: honor ה׳ first.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל both learn from ישעיהו 2:22 that one should not greet a person before praying. רב reads בַּמֶּה as בָּמָה, while שמואל keeps the plain reading as a rebuke.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
How did you consider this one important,
and not God?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בַּמֶּה חֲשַׁבְתּוֹ לָזֶה וְלֹא לָאֱלוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק that רב used in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק, read plainly, rebukes someone who honored a person before ה׳.

steps.title: רב ששת's challenge from greeting during קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת challenges רב's teaching against greeting before praying. Our משנה lets a person greet someone out of respect even during the breaks of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raises an objection: in the breaks between the paragraphs, a person may greet someone out of respect, and may answer a greeting!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב's rule from step 16. Our משנה lets a person greet others out of respect during קריאת שמע, and קריאת שמע comes before praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said greeting someone before praying is like making him into a בָּמָה. But the משנה lets you greet people during קריאת שמע, which is said before תפילה. So how can greeting before תפילה be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: The breaks between the paragraphs of קריאת שמע

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
In the breaks, one may greet out of respect, and respond!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's teaching from step 16 against greeting before praying.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that greeting a friend before praying is like making him a בָּמָה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קריאת שמע comes before תפילה, yet the משנה allows greeting out of respect during it. So greeting before תפילה should not be forbidden.

steps.title: Only going early to his door is the problem
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that רב only forbade going out early to someone's door just to greet him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא explained it: it is talking about someone who goes early to his door.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers רב ששת's challenge. רב was only talking about someone who goes out early to another person's door to greet him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different cases. If you just bump into someone, you may greet him, as the משנה says. But making a special early trip to his house to greet him, before you have greeted ה׳ in תפילה, is what רב forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: Gets up early, goes out early

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba explained it:
When one goes early to his door.
phrases.notes: He means making a special early trip to someone's house just to greet him. Simply meeting someone is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge by narrowing רב's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: רב's rule is only about a special early visit to greet someone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed רב forbade any greeting before praying, which would clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only going early to someone's door to greet him is forbidden. A greeting by chance, like in the משנה, is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Before praying in the morning, don't make a special trip to greet someone. Greeting someone you happen to meet is not the problem.

steps.title: Taking care of your business before praying is like building an altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה quotes רבי זירא: whoever takes care of his own affairs before praying is like someone who built a בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה said that רבי זירא said: anyone who takes care of his own affairs before he prays, it is as if he built an altar.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. Taking care of your own business before תפילה is compared to building a בָּמָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes past greeting people and covers all of a person's own affairs. It uses the same strong "altar" language that רב used in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: An altar (here, one built outside the proper place)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yona said that Rabbi Zeira said:
Anyone who takes care of his own affairs before he prays —
It is as if he built an altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from greeting people to taking care of one's own affairs before praying, using similar language.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking care of your own affairs before praying is like building a בָּמָה.

steps.title: Did you really say 'an altar'?
steps.stepSummary: The listeners ask רבי יונה whether he really said 'a בָּמָה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did you say 'an altar'?
steps.whatsHappening: The listeners are surprised by the strong word and check what רבי יונה really said. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing someone to a person who built a בָּמָה is very harsh. So they want to know whether this was the exact wording.

phrases.english: They said to him: did you say "an altar"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the exact wording of the teaching in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יונה really used the word בָּמָה.

steps.title: No, I only said it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה answers that he did not say 'altar'. He only said it is אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: No, I said it is 'forbidden.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונה corrects how they heard him. The teaching is simply that taking care of your affairs before praying is אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harsh "altar" comparison is dropped. What is left is a plain rule: it is not allowed, without the extra picture of building a בָּמָה.

phrases.english: He said to them: No,
I said "forbidden."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching is only that it is אסור, not that it is like building a בָּמָה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't come away thinking it is now allowed. רבי יונה only took back the harsh "altar" wording. He still says it is אסור.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין: forbidden to take care of your affairs before praying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב אידי בר אבין in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: a person may not take care of his own affairs before praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: (And this is like what רב אידי בר אבין said:) רב אידי בר אבין said that רב יצחק בר אשיאן said: a person is forbidden to take care of his own affairs before he prays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא who says the same rule: it is אסור to take care of your affairs before you pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up רבי יונה's corrected version from step 23. The plain word אסור is exactly what this teaching uses.

keyTerms.meaning: To take care of his own affairs

phrases.english: (And like Rav Idi bar Avin, who said)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. With them, the line ties this teaching to רבי יונה's answer.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָאן:
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said that Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan said:
A person is forbidden to take care of his own affairs
before he prays,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יונה's corrected wording, 'forbidden,' with another teaching that says the same.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is אסור for a person to take care of his own affairs before he prays.

steps.title: The פסוק: righteousness goes first
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned from a פסוק in תהלים: "Righteousness shall go before Him, and shall make His footsteps on a path."
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Righteousness shall go before Him, and shall make His footsteps on a path."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source in the פסוקים for the rule that you may not take care of your affairs before praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First comes "righteousness": praying and recognizing ה׳'s righteousness. Only after that does a person "set his footsteps on a path," heading out to his own business. The order in the פסוק becomes the order of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is said: "Righteousness shall go before Him,
and shall make His footsteps on a path."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״צֶדֶק לְפָנָיו יְהַלֵּךְ וְיָשֵׂם לְדֶרֶךְ פְּעָמָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוקים for רב אידי בר אבין's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that it is אסור to take care of your affairs before praying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 85:14: righteousness comes first, and only then does one set out on his path.
steps.whatToRemember: In the morning, תפילה comes first. Your own business comes after.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the הלכה that a person should not start his own work or business in the morning before he has prayed.

steps.title: Pray first, then travel, and God takes care of your needs
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין, in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן, teaches that whoever prays and only afterward sets out on a journey will have his needs taken care of by הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: Anyone who prays first and only then goes out on the road, the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes care of his needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same speakers as step 24. This time it is a positive promise: pray first, then travel, and God handles your affairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 was a warning: don't take care of your own business before praying. This step gives the reward for doing it the right way. Someone who puts תפילה first does not lose out. Instead, God takes care of the very affairs he put off.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets out on the road / goes on a journey
The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)

phrases.english: And Rav Idi bar Avin said
Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan said:
Anyone who prays and afterward
goes out on the road,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ חֲפָצָיו,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes care of his needs,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same speakers. It turns the warning of step 24 into a positive promise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prays before setting out on a journey has his needs taken care of by הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: The proof from the same verse in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: The promise is proven from the פסוק 'צדק לפניו יהלך וישם לדרך פעמיו'. Righteousness (prayer) goes first, and then God sets his steps on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Righteousness shall go before him, and he shall set his footsteps on the road.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the promise of step 26 from the same פסוק it used in step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the פסוק showed the order: צדק (prayer) must come first. Here the second half, 'וישם לדרך פעמיו', is read as the reward. After the prayer, God guides his steps on the journey and takes care of his needs.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)

phrases.english: as it is said: 'Righteousness shall go before him,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 85:14. This is the same פסוק as in step 25.

phrases.english: and he shall set his footsteps on the road.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the promise in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The promise that one who prays before traveling has his needs taken care of.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 85:14: 'צדק לפניו יהלך וישם לדרך פעמיו'.

steps.title: Seven nights without a dream
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה, in the name of רבי זירא, teaches that a person who sleeps seven nights without dreaming is called 'רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יונה said in the name of רבי זירא: Anyone who sleeps seven nights without a dream is called 'evil'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי יונה in the name of רבי זירא, the same pair who spoke in step 21. It says that someone who goes seven nights with no dream is called 'רע'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, dreams. It comes up here only because the speakers were just mentioned. The teaching is short: someone who goes a full week without any dream is given the label 'רע'. The source in the פסוק comes in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic, not part of the rules about תפילה. The גמרא brings it only because רבי יונה and רבי זירא were just quoted in step 21.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yona said in the name of Rabbi Zeira:
Anyone who sleeps seven nights
without a dream
is called 'evil',

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic. It is linked only by the speakers, who were mentioned in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who goes seven nights without a dream is called 'רע'.

steps.title: Reading 'satisfied' as 'seven'
steps.stepSummary: The teaching is drawn from משלי 19:23. The word 'שָׂבֵעַ' (satisfied) is reread as 'שֶׁבַע' (seven): one who sleeps seven nights and is not visited is 'רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He sleeps satisfied, he is not visited, evil.' Do not read שָׂבֵעַ (satisfied) but שֶׁבַע (seven).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבי זירא's teaching. It uses a פסוק and rereads one word in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reading שֶׁבַע (seven) instead of שָׂבֵעַ (satisfied), the פסוק becomes: 'He sleeps seven nights, he is not visited, he is evil.' 'Not visited' is understood as not being visited by a dream. So the word 'רע' is attached to that person.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read [it as]... but rather [as]... (rereading a word to learn a teaching)

phrases.english: as it is said: 'He sleeps satisfied,'
'he will not be visited, evil.'
phrases.notes: Here 'not visited' means no dream came to him. 'Evil' is read as what he is called.

phrases.english: Do not read 'savea' (satisfied)
but rather 'sheva' (seven).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 28's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That one who goes seven nights without a dream is called 'רע'.

steps.title: רב אחא's different version: sleeping full of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, says the real teaching, from רבי יוחנן, reads the same פסוק differently. One who fills himself with Torah and goes to sleep will not be told bad news.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said to him: This is what רבי חייא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who fills himself with words of Torah and goes to sleep, they do not bring him bad news, as it says: 'He sleeps satisfied, he will not be visited by evil.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא responds to רבי יונה. He says the teaching he received reads the פסוק in a completely different, positive way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא keeps the plain word 'שָׂבֵעַ' (satisfied) and does not change it to 'seven'. 'Satisfied' means full of Torah. 'Not visited by evil' means no bad news reaches him. So the same פסוק turns from a description of someone 'רע' into a promise of protection.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [he] said (introduces the correct version of a teaching)
One who fills himself / makes himself full

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק, 'ושבע ילין בל יפקד רע', is read two ways. רבי זירא changes 'satisfied' to 'seven' and gets a negative description: seven nights with no dream. רבי יוחנן keeps 'satisfied' and gets a promise: whoever sleeps full of Torah gets no bad news.

phrases.english: Rav Acha said to him
the son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
This is what Rabbi Chiyya said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Anyone who fills himself
with words of Torah and goes to sleep,
they do not announce to him
bad news,
as it is said: 'He sleeps satisfied,'
'he will not be visited by evil.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבי יונה's reading of the פסוק by offering another version and a different meaning.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'seven nights without a dream' reading of the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to the version from רבי יוחנן, the פסוק keeps 'שָׂבֵעַ' as 'satisfied' and is a positive promise about Torah, not a negative label.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who goes to sleep filled with Torah is not told bad news.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the breaks between the sections
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next line, 'אלו הן בין הפרקים', to start discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These are [the breaks] between the sections, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא leaves the side topics and quotes the next part of the משנה, getting ready to discuss it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the places 'between the sections' of קריאת שמע and its ברכות where a person may interrupt in certain cases. The גמרא only quotes the opening words. The real discussion of this line comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Between the sections (the breaks between the parts of קריאת שמע and its ברכות)
Etc. (the rest of the quote is not written out)
The core teaching the גמרא is explaining

phrases.english: These are [the breaks] between the sections, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the side discussion and goes back to the משנה to open a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the discussion of the משנה's list of breaks 'between the sections'.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: no stopping before אמת ויציב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. One may not interrupt between ״אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״ and ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה, who said that you may not stop between ״אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״ and ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling. In the dispute over whether the spot between the end of שמע and אמת ויציב counts as a break, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״ is the last word of קריאת שמע, and ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״ is the first words of the ברכה after it. Normally the point between two sections counts as a ״בין הפרקים״ break. רבי יהודה treats this one spot differently: here you may not interrupt at all, and רבי יוחנן rules this way as the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law, how we actually act
He will interrupt or stop (for example, to greet someone)
"Your God": the last word of קריאת שמע
"True and certain": the opening of the ברכה after the morning שמע

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling about how we say שמע today. We go straight from the end of שמע into אמת without a break.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda
who said that between "Eloheichem" and "Emet Veyatziv"
phrases.notes: ״אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״ is how שמע ends, and ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״ is how the next ברכה begins, so this is the seam between them.

phrases.english: one may not interrupt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after quoting the משנה's line about the breaks, the גמרא gives the practical ruling on the dispute in it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: no interruption between ״אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״ and ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן begins to give רבי יהודה's reason from a verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, asks what רבי יהודה's reason is. He starts to answer with "as it is written", and the פסוק follows right after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי יהודה's reason? Because it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now explains why רבי יהודה rules this way. This line sets up the next move: the פסוק that serves as the source comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in the last step is now given a source. The question "מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ" is not an attack. רבי יוחנן asks it so that he can answer it himself with a פסוק that ties the end of שמע to the word אמת.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (a פסוק is about to be quoted)

steps.confusionAlert: "מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ" here is not a challenge against רבי יהודה. It is just a request for his source, and רבי יוחנן answers it himself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
